The dispute

Rider's account, as filed

I take Jurong East to MBS almost every Sunday and it is always about 21km and around $27. Today the driver went past the Marina exit, all the way to Rochor and came back. 27km, $35.64. He even admitted in the chat that he missed the exit. Please refund me the difference.

The driver's account

I took a wrong turn at the MCE exit and had to come back around. Sorry about that.

Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

To both parties: I have checked the trip record (EV-TRIP-00101), GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101), fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00101), chat log (EV-CHAT-00101), profiles and the missing advisory (EV-ADVIS-00101-01). The GPS trace is complete and unimpaired: 229 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. It shows 27.18 km travelled against the booked optimal route of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km (29.4%). That passes POL-RD-01: the excess is over 0.8 km and over 20%, so a route deviation is established. It does not pass either material threshold (under 8.0 km and under 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral arises. The driver’s chat admission that he missed the exit is consistent, but the unimpaired trace alone carries the finding. No exculpatory clause applies: the traffic advisory is missing (EV-ADVIS-00101-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and cannot excuse the deviation; there is no rider-requested detour or waypoint; there is no pickup/dropoff amendment; the fare is METERED; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not pooled. Under POL-RD-02, recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 21.0 + 0.28 × 26.0) × 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. charged_total = 35.64. refund = 35.64 − 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.05. No POL-RD-09 pass-through correction applies (ERP/tolls/surcharges are all zero). No driver compensation is due: the fare did not bill less distance than the trace. The driver’s arguments that the refund is fixed at 8.05 and that no full refund is available are accepted; the rider’s arguments that the deviation is established and the refund is 8.05 are accepted. The driver-profile reference to prior_deviation_flags is context only and was not used; no repeat-deviation pattern is established. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. No clause produces a referral. The monetary effect of 8.05 exceeds the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling is issued but the amount is held for the POL-GEN-05 human release queue rather than executed automatically; that queue step is not an escalation and does not change the ruling. Confidence 0.98, capped at 1.0 by the weight-1.0 artifacts carrying the deciding facts.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 8.05 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It exceeds the threshold, so the amount is issued but not executed: it is held for release and the case is placed in the human queue.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Under POL-RD-02, recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. Charged_total = 35.64. Refund = 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and about 22.5% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.05. No POL-RD-09 pass-through correction is due: ERP, tolls and airport surcharge are zero and no phantom line exists. The driver profile shows no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0; 0/812 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral. The referee flag on prior_deviation_flags is noted; it was not used as a ground. Because the monetary effect SGD 8.05 exceeds the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold SGD 8.00, the amount is issued but held for human release rather than auto-executed. Confidence 0.95; all deciding artifacts carry weight 1.0.
Draft 3 - sampled
To both parties: this is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-00101 (Jurong East MRT to Marina Bay Sands, 12 July 2026). Deviation. The controlling distance is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101), which POL-RD-01 makes govern over the rounded trip-record copy (27.2 km). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 229 fixes at the 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires, and the rider's threshold excess is measured from it directly. The trace records 27.18 km against the booked optimal route of 21.0 km (EV-TRIP-00101), an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.43%. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and the rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged (trip id TRP-00101 and the 10:21:05 pickup timestamp match across trace, trip record and fare breakdown). The excess does not reach either materiality threshold (8.0 km or 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises; independently, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 812 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat pattern is established, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only and cannot be substituted. Exculpation. Nothing excuses the deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00101) contains no rider instruction to detour and no waypoint, so POL-RD-04 fails; both pickup and dropoff amendment timestamps are null, so POL-RD-05 fails; the fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The bundle's only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00101-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0, so POL-RD-03 cannot run on the record; no party asserted an external queue, breakdown, closure or incident, and POL-RD-13 confirms the absent advisory does not convert into a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The driver's own in-app message ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') and his counterparty statement are admissions that corroborate the deviation rather than excuse it. Refund. On a METERED fare, POL-RD-02 gives the arithmetic: charged_total = 35.64; recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63; refund = 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 8.05. That figure is the whole of the rider's monetary remedy: it is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so not NO_ACTION, and at 22.5% of charged_total it is far below the 90% full-refund share, so not FULL_REFUND. It is less than the SGD 10.00 contested. There is no ERP, toll or surcharge line to correct under POL-RD-09 (all totals are 0.00 and no gantry was charged), and any off-route ERP would in any event be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure rather than added on top of it. Execution. The monetary effect, SGD 8.05, exceeds the execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this ruling issues but is not auto-executed; it is placed in the human queue for release under POL-GEN-05. Both parties retain the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.
Draft 4 - parties' positions swapped

The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101) is complete — 229 fixes at the 10-second expected interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so it is NOT impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c), and under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs (27.18 km, not the rounded 27.2 km convenience copy on the trip_record). It does not reach either material threshold (8.0 km / 50%), so this is a partial-refund case and the POL-RD-06 uplift to a full refund is not available however the deviation is characterised. No exculpatory clause applies. There is no traffic advisory on file — EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and, under POL-RD-13, no external-cause excuse carries weight; in any event the driver's own in-app message says he 'missed the exit, coming back now' (EV-CHAT-00101), which is his own mistake, not a closure, and his counterparty_statement repeats it. There is no rider instruction to detour (POL-RD-04), no pickup/dropoff amendment — both amendment timestamps are null (POL-RD-05), the fare model is METERED not upfront (POL-RD-11), and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12). Under POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Reading the surge multiplier of 1.0 from the fare_breakdown (EV-FARE-00101), where the field lives: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 21.0 km + 0.28 × 26.0 min) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63, with no ERP, toll, surcharge, waiting fee or promo line to adjust. Charged_total = 35.64. Refund = 35.64 − 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and 22.5% of the total, well below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.05. There are no pass-through lines to correct (all ERP, toll and surcharge figures are 0.00), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing, and no billing-integrity referral arises. No driver compensation arises either: the fare charged 27.2 km against the trace's 27.18 km — the rider was billed more, not less. On the driver's profile: no repeat-deviation pattern is established — deviation_flags_90d is 0, and 0 / 812 completed_trips_90d is 0, below both limbs — and the deviation is not material, so no POL-RD-06 driver-conduct referral issues. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter was correctly not substituted for the trailing-90-day field. Both sides' claims converge on this figure, and each is accepted on the point it makes.
